articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document, titled "EPHEMERIS," is identified as Volume 3, Number 2 of the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It was published in February 1991, serving as a regular newsletter or journal for the organization.

articles.title: BOARD ELECTIONS!
articles.summary: The SJAA will hold board elections at its February 2nd General Meeting, where five members will be elected to two-year terms on the nine-member Board of Directors. Nominations are open from the committee and the floor. The elected Board will then select officers for one-year terms.

articles.title: SLIDE SHOW
articles.summary: Following upcoming elections, Bob Fingerhut will host a slide show event featuring three presentations. One of these will showcase Space Art by the renowned Chesley Bonestell, who was honored with Asteroid 3129 shortly before his death in 1986.

articles.title: STAR PARTIES THIS MONTH
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting multiple star parties this month. Events include a party at Grant Ranch/Halls Valley on February 9th, a New Moon star party at Fremont Peak State Park on February 16th, and a public star party at Branham Lane Park on February 22nd. Attendees are reminded that all events are weather permitting and directions are available via their "Hot" line.

articles.title: BOARD MEETING REMINDER
articles.summary: The SJAA Board Meetings have been rescheduled to take place before the General Meetings at 6:30. All members of the San Jose Astronomical Association are invited and welcome to attend these board meetings.

articles.title: ASTROPHOTO IX
articles.summary: The article announces the Astrophoto IX conference on March 30 in Thousand Oaks, covering celestial photography for all skill levels, sponsored by Ventura County Astronomical and Orange County Astronomers. It also lists several upcoming events in February and early March, including general meetings, board elections, star parties at various locations, and an observational astronomy class.

articles.title: SJAA HOTLINE
articles.summary: The article announces an astrophotography seminar, likely hosted by the Ventura County Astronomical Society, featuring lectures, workshops, new equipment displays, vendor booths, and a professional-level photo exhibit. Attracting hundreds of amateur astrophotographers, it offers a full day of learning from leading experts. Preregistration, including proceedings, costs $20.

articles.title: SPACE PROGRAM UPDATE
articles.summary: The ASTRO-1 Spacelab mission, aboard the Space Shuttle Columbia, successfully made 400 observations of 135 targets, exceeding pre-launch objectives despite significant technical issues with onboard systems. Its four telescopes (HUT, UIT, WUPPE, BBXRT) yielded remarkable data, including detailed observations of Jupiter and Io, the binary star Z-Cam, imaging of new galaxies and white dwarfs, insights into star formation, and the first high-quality X-ray spectrum of NGC 1399's gas halo. The Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRSS) was critical in enabling ground control to manage the mission given the onboard failures.

articles.title: GALILEO AND MAGELLAN PROVIDE DATA ABOUT VENUS
articles.summary: The Galileo probe returned high-resolution data on Venus' middle cloud deck, potentially offering insights into the planet's unusually fast atmospheric rotation and the presence of lightning. Meanwhile, the Magellan mission has completed approximately one-third of its radar mapping of Venus' surface, revealing an absence of small craters, which suggests recent volcanic resurfacing and contradicts earlier theories of an ancient, volcanically inactive surface.

articles.title: GALILEO EXPLORES THE EARTH/ MOON SYSTEM
articles.summary: During its Earth flyby on December 8, 1990, the Galileo spacecraft captured novel observations of the Moon, including unprecedented views of the Orientale Basin and the South Pole-Aitken Basin. Spectroscopic analysis of the South Pole-Aitken Basin indicated a high iron content, suggesting a deep impact that exposed mantle material. Galileo also created a time-lapse movie of Earth's rotation during this period.

articles.title: NASA BREAKTHROUGH WITH DRUG TO CURE SPACE SICKNESS
articles.summary: NASA researchers have discovered that the drug promethazine, when injected on the first day of a space flight, effectively eliminates severe symptoms of space motion sickness, with astronauts becoming symptom-free by the second day. This breakthrough treatment has been administered to astronauts 14 times since 1988.

articles.title: EXPLORING IN LYNX
articles.summary: Steve Gottlieb's article "EXPLORING IN LYNX" describes the challenges and rewards of deep-sky observing in the constellation Lynx, a region notably devoid of bright stars. Despite navigation difficulties, he highlights fascinating objects like the distant globular cluster NGC 2419, the bright edge-on galaxy NGC 2683, the unusual "Bearpaw" galaxy NGC 2537, and the rich Abell 779 galaxy cluster, offering personal observing notes for each.

articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This article details several deep-sky observing reports, focusing on the NGC 2832 galaxy cluster, the planetary nebula Jones-Emberson 1, and the double stars 12 Lyncis and 71338. It describes visual characteristics, observational challenges, recommended equipment (like OIII filters), and historical notes for these celestial objects. The author shares personal experiences and techniques for resolving faint or close targets using various telescope apertures and magnifications.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The article provides an update on comet activity, noting the recent discovery of a new faint and a new bright comet, alongside the continued visibility of Periodic Comet Wild 2 and Comet Levy. It details the reclassification of Periodic Comet Shoemaker-Levy 2 from an asteroid due to its observed tail and announces the discovery of Comet Brewington (1991a), while also reflecting on 1990 as a modest year for new comet finds.

articles.title: METEOR NOTES
articles.summary: This article, 'METEOR NOTES,' provides a detailed forecast for major meteor showers occurring during the remainder of 1991, specifically tailored for observers in the San Jose area. It includes key data such as maximum dates, local maximum times, radiant locations, expected rates, and moon conditions, along with an overall outlook for each shower. The author emphasizes that the maximum times refer to local maximums based on radiant elevation, not global stream passage.

articles.title: SHOWER: LEONIDS
articles.summary: This document provides details for observing the Leonids meteor shower, specifically on November 17, 1991, at 5:07 AM PST. It includes observation location coordinates, an estimated local rate of 10 meteors per hour, and notes that the moon had set, indicating good viewing conditions.

articles.title: SHOWER: GEMINIDS
articles.summary: This document details an observation report for the Geminids meteor shower, which peaked on December 14, 1991, at 2:11 AM PST. Observers noted an excellent outlook with the Moon having set, recording a local rate of 60 meteors per hour from a specific sky location.

articles.title: SHOWER: URSIDS
articles.summary: This document details the Ursids meteor shower, specifically forecasting its peak on December 22, 1991. It provides observational parameters such as the maximum date and time (5:30 AM PST), location, a local rate of 10 meteors/hour, moon rise time, and a "poor" outlook for viewing.

articles.title: OFFICERS AND BOARD OF DIRECTORS
articles.summary: This document provides a list of the current officers and board of directors for an organization. It details the names and contact phone numbers for individuals holding key leadership roles, including President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, Editor, and several Directors.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS CONTRIBUTORS
articles.summary: This document lists individuals who are contributors to an ephemeris, providing their names and, in most cases, their contact phone numbers. It serves as a directory for these contributors, with some contact details noted as incomplete.

articles.title: COMET EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is titled "COMET EPHEMERIS" and presents a table structure for tracking a comet's position and brightness over time. The table includes columns for date, right ascension and declination for two different epochs (1950 and 2000), elongation, sky conditions, and visual magnitude. It serves as a format or placeholder for detailed astronomical data related to comet observations.

articles.title: Periodic Comet Wild 2 (1989t)
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet Wild 2 (1989t), detailing its predicted celestial positions (right ascension and declination) and visual magnitudes. The data covers a period from late January to early March, serving as a guide for astronomers and observers to locate and track the comet.

articles.title: Comet Levy (1990c)
articles.summary: This document presents observational data for Comet Levy (1990c). It contains a table detailing the comet's right ascension, declination, position angle, and magnitude, recorded on various dates from late January to early March. This data serves as an ephemeris or a log of its observed positions and brightness over time.

articles.title: THIS MONTH'S METEORS
articles.summary: This document, titled 'THIS MONTH'S METEORS', presents an ephemeris for upcoming meteor showers. It details the Delta Leonids, Virginids, and Delta Normids, providing information such as their active dates, date of maximum, maximum visual zenithal rate, radiant point coordinates (R.A. and DEC), velocity, and additional notes for each shower. The content serves as a guide for observing these celestial events.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS provides a free classifieds service for non-commercial advertisers to sell astronomy-related products and services, with submissions due by the 15th of each month for a three-month run. The document then lists several example advertisements, featuring a variety of used astronomical equipment such as telescopes, binoculars, filters, finderscopes, and related accessories like video digitizer boards and scientific calculators. Items are offered by individuals with contact information and asking prices.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION
articles.summary: This document is a membership application for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining various membership tiers including general, S&T magazine inclusive, and junior memberships. It provides instructions for submitting the application and payment to the treasurer. Additionally, it contains contact information for the SJAA's monthly publication, "SJAA Ephemeris," and guidelines for article submissions.
